title: 2020 AMC 10A 15
statement: A positive integer divisor of \(12!\) is chosen at random. The probability that the divisor chosen is a perfect square can be expressed as \(\frac{m}{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(m+n?\)

solutions.text:
The prime factorization of \(12!\) is \(2^{10}3^5 5^2 7^1 11^1\). Therefore \(12!\) has \((10+1)(5+1)\) \(\cdot(2+1)(1+1)(1+1)=792\) positive divisors.

A square divisor must use only even exponents, giving \(6\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1\cdot1=36\) square divisors. The probability is \(\frac{36}{792}=\frac{1}{22}\), so \(m+n=1+22=23\). Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: A square divisor must choose only even prime exponents
